comments.author: @travellives
comments.text: If you grew up in Saint Lucia, what was the first thing your family bought at Castries Market on a Saturday? I’d love to hear what you took home and who usually cooked it.

comments.author: @lifeonearth68
comments.text: I never really thought about how different fishing could be on opposite sides of the same small island. Does the rougher Atlantic side make fishing a lot harder for local crews?

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Thank you! Yes, the Atlantic side, like the waters off Dennery, is definitely more exposed. It turns every fishing trip into a much tougher calculation of weather, safety, and fuel costs compared to the sheltered Caribbean bays. It really shows how adaptable and resilient the local crews have to be!

comments.author: @TravelThePlanet68
comments.text: St. Lucia looks like paradise, but I believe the real beauty lies in how ordinary people live beyond the luxury resorts. Would you choose a peaceful life on this volcanic island over a busy city?

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: The true heartbeat of Saint Lucia is found in its local communities, vibrant markets, and quiet fishing bays. As for choosing it over a city—it's a beautiful trade-off. You leave behind city convenience for a deep, genuine connection to the land, history, and neighbors.

comments.author: @ZechariahWoodward-d7m
comments.text: Surrounded by the ocean on all sides, yet the island faces water shortages every dry season. Such an ironic struggle

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: As we saw during the 2024 dry period, it completely changes how families have to plan their daily lives

comments.author: @RodriguezEvelyn-l4g
comments.text: Looks like paradise on the outside, but having to import almost everything must make daily life there pretty tough

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Spot on, Evelyn. While the island produces wonderful fresh food—as we see at Castries Market—relying on imported goods for other daily necessities means families are always vulnerable to fluctuating transport and fuel costs.

comments.author: @WilliamsOliver-z1d
comments.text: Driving those narrow mountain roads every single day must take serious skill

replies.author: @MonteEdmunds
replies.text: That is when you are a driver or not.

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: That’s right—they carry out that high-risk work every single day.
